limits: Everything in the file's metadata is declared by the file and can be edited or copied from another photo.
A phone or camera model is shared by millions of devices: it never identifies one device.
WhatsApp, Instagram, X, Facebook and most other platforms remove or rewrite metadata when media is uploaded, so missing metadata is normal and proves nothing either way.
Only a sensor-noise (PRNU) comparison against photos from a specific suspected camera can link an image to a physical device, and resizing or social-media processing usually destroys that signal.

device.note: This is normal for social-media copies and for AI-generated images. It does not mean the media is real or fake.

limits: This tests a specific suspected camera against reference photos; it never identifies a camera on its own.
A camera MODEL is not a device. Only reference photos from the suspected physical device can support a match.
Resizing, cropping, heavy JPEG compression and social-media processing weaken or destroy the pattern.
AI-generated images have no sensor pattern. A non-match says nothing about whether media is real.
